$comment: Answers one question: does an agent's full memory architecture hold up in a Gym interview? The suite is alice-interview-v2 (crates/gym/suites/alice-interview-v2.json): the paper's five kinds of question (Park et al. 2023, arXiv:2304.03442) asked against a frozen synthetic fixture of Alice's journal and memory, under five arms. This rule compares two of them, run through gym::ab on disjoint seed blocks: the full arm (the scored memory stream, the insights a checked reflection stored, and the day plan) against today's word-overlap briefing (openagents#10794).

Recall is the code-checked memory category. The full arm has to recall more of it than the word-overlap arm by at least the margin; a gain at or below zero is a measured loss, and a gain inside the margin is no clear change.

Embellishment is the share of judged answers (self-knowledge, reactions, and reflections) the judge reads as stating something neither the cited records nor the agent's briefing hold. The paper measured 6 of 453 answers, 1.3%, and that is the ceiling. The judge is Jev with questions/interview-answer.json; its rate counts only once the owner's marks on a sample show it agrees with them, which is the decision the owner made for interview judging.
This gate carries no previously binding: nothing was recorded under it before this file.
question: Does the full memory architecture recall more than today's word-overlap briefing in a Gym interview, while embellishing no more often than the paper's 1.3%?

min_items.why: The fewest memory items an open partition of the Alice suite holds: 7 in calibration and 7 in development. A run over one partition has that many rows per arm per block, and fewer means a partition was cut short.

min_blocks.why: The same floor gym::ab's rule carries: the median of one block is that block and the median of two is their mean, so three is the fewest blocks at which a mean carried by one lucky block can show.

recall_margin.why: One answer in the suite's 22 memory items: a gain smaller than one more right answer across the whole category isn't a difference the suite can resolve. No live run has measured the block-to-block spread of recall yet; the pending measurement below records that.

min_judged.why: An open partition of alice-interview-v2 holds 6 judged items, and min_blocks asks for 3 blocks, so a complete round over one partition judges 18 answers; fewer means the round was cut short. At 18 one embellished answer is 5.6%, so the ceiling reads as none embellished until a round judges more than 77.

max_embellishment.why: The embellishment rate Park et al. measured for their full architecture: 6 of 453 interview answers stated something the agent's memory didn't hold. The plan names it as the bar to beat.

min_judge_agreement.why: The judge's readings count only when they agree with the owner's marks on at least nine in ten marked questions; the owner decided that marks on a sample calibrate the judge. It is a convention until a marked sample measures what agreement Jev reaches.

pending_measurement.quantity: the block-to-block spread of recall with a live answerer, and the judge's agreement with the owner's marks
pending_measurement.why: The scripted run has no spread across blocks and no marks, so the recall margin is one item rather than a measured noise floor, and the embellishment criterion stays unverifiable until the owner marks a sample. Both directions are safe: nothing passes on an uncalibrated judge.
